snapshots.rainwater_initial:
A Rainwater Helper for Our School Garden

My idea is a rainwater helper for our school garden. Roof water flows into a tall barrel. A screen catches leaves. Then the water moves through a cloth filter and into a small tank.

When the soil feels dry, a student opens a valve. Water travels through a hose to the garden beds. This could help us use less tap water.

Extra water leaves through an overflow pipe and goes into the school drain.
snapshots.rainwater_revision:
A Rainwater Helper for Our School Garden

My idea is a rainwater helper for our school garden. Roof water flows into a tall barrel. A screen catches leaves. Students empty the screen into our yard-waste container after the leaves dry. Then the water moves through a cloth filter and into a small tank.

When the soil feels dry, a student opens a valve. Water travels through a hose to the garden beds. This could help us use less tap water.

Extra water leaves through an overflow pipe and goes into the school drain.
snapshots.paper_bridge:
How to Test a Paper Bridge

Fold a sheet of paper into a long accordion shape. Place the two ends on equal stacks of books, leaving a gap between the stacks. The folds give the paper a shape that can resist bending.

Put one washer in the center of the bridge. Keep adding washers one at a time until the paper touches the table or falls. Count only the washers the bridge held before it collapsed.

Repeat the test with a flat sheet and another accordion sheet with wider folds. Use the same paper size, book gap, and washers each time. Compare the counts to see which shape held the most weight.
snapshots.compost_optional:
How Our Class Compost Bin Works

We collect fruit peels, vegetable scraps, and dry leaves in separate classroom containers. We cut the scraps into smaller pieces so they have more exposed surfaces. We do not add meat, dairy, or plastic.

We add one layer of scraps and then one layer of dry leaves to the bin. A student turns the mixture with a garden fork each week. We check that it feels like a wrung-out sponge and add dry leaves if it is too wet.

Over time, the mixture becomes dark and crumbly. We remove any pieces that still need more time and put the finished compost around garden plants. Our chart records the date and the materials we add each week.
snapshots.library_argument:
Our school library should open thirty minutes before classes. In the assigned survey, 32 of 45 students said they would use the library then to read or finish homework. This proves that opening early would raise grades.

An early opening would also give students a quiet place without changing class schedules.
snapshots.library_revision:
Our school library should open thirty minutes before classes. In the assigned survey, 32 of 45 students said they would use the library then to read or finish homework. This shows interest in an early opening, but it does not prove a change in grades.

An early opening would give those students a regular quiet place to read or finish work without changing class schedules.
snapshots.umbrella_initial:
The Yellow Umbrella

The rain started right when I left for the bus stop. I opened my yellow umbrella, but one spoke flipped backward. "Seriously?" I said, and my little brother laughed so hard he almost dropped his backpack.

I tried to push the spoke down. My brother stopped laughing and held my backpack for me. Then I remembered the rubber band on my lunch bag.
snapshots.umbrella_revision:
The Yellow Umbrella

The rain started right when I left for the bus stop. I opened my yellow umbrella, but one spoke flipped backward. "Seriously?" I said, and my little brother laughed so hard he almost dropped his backpack.

I tried to push the spoke down. My brother stopped laughing and held my backpack for me. Then I remembered the rubber band on my lunch bag. I looped it around the loose spoke and the handle. The umbrella still looked crooked, but we squeezed under it and hurried to the bus stop together.
